declared.title: The misinformation effect: A contemporary replication and extension of Loftus et al. (1978) to investigate its underlying mechanisms.
declared.venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
declared.foundIn: Europe PMC search « ("misinformation effect" OR "misleading postevent information" OR "post-event misinformation") AND (replication OR preregistered OR "registered report") » (2026-11-23)

population: adults tested online in three experiments (a car-accident video, then co-witness statements); sample sizes and country not in the abstract

findings.text: People who later read misleading statements from other witnesses reported the traffic sign they had actually seen less often than controls

support.sentence: Misled participants reported the correct sign less often than controls.

findings.text: With a four-option test and points bet on confidence, the effect was still found, though smaller; two things changed at once (the test format and the stakes)

support.sentence: With an identical procedure but a four-option memory test and confidence-based point betting, we still found the effect, though smaller.

findings.text: Going along with the experimenter does not explain the whole effect

support.sentence: Hence, demand effects are not the sole driver of the misinformation effect.

findings.text: The authors conclude the effect is robust, partly driven by answering as one thinks is expected, and largely, not definitively, explained by the original being replaced or blocked

support.sentence: In conclusion, our studies confirmed memory's susceptibility to misinformation, showing a robust effect partly driven by demand effects and largely, though not definitively, explained by single-trace or blocking mechanisms.

limits: an online study with a car-accident video made in a video game: a lab event, not one's own life
full text closed, not read: sample sizes and country unknown; authors in the Netherlands, Belgium, Israel and the US (an Israeli sample would not be Arab)
the smaller effect with four options and betting changes the test format and the stakes together: how much is « going along » is not isolated
